Title: [OT] plugs for two dam' fine games

Messages.Author: legb...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
Thanks to Prescott and LSJ i got to play two very fine games* in the USA
which WEREN'T Jyhad/VTES, namely Fairy Meat [Kenzer games] and Vinci
[Descartes]. Fairy meat is possibly the world's first 1:1 scale
miniatures game, VERY vampiric and one of the funniest i've ever played.
Vinci is sort of all the best bits of civilisation, Britannia and Cosmic
Encounter all rolled into one, and it has an epic quality which should
appeal to the Methuselah mind. When we played it the most civilised
Methuselah turned out to be David Tatu. There's a kind of rightness about
that, i obscurely feel.

*Actually i got to play several other good games but i was so drunk that
i can't even remember their names. Fairly sure i lost at all of them
though. There was a good one with fancy marbles, called Zvrt or something
equally bizarre. LSJ kicked my arse at that one, for sure.

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

Did you guys ever play Arcadia/Wyld Hunt or King Ironheart's Madness?
They were made by White Wolf and were basically a collectible card-game
version of Talisman, it seemed to me. Excellent artwork [except for the
Leagues - yeuch!], easy to learn and very funny, especially KIHM -
Affectionate Oil Slick, Pathetic Snivelling, Proselytising Velociraptors
and the Newt Gingrich Spoof [Speakers?] being possibly my favourite cards
for any CCG of all time ever. Not quite sure why they never took off -
something to do with negative tactics against the other players being
overpowered, perhaps, or maybe it's just that NOBODY except my friend
Marianne wants to play at being a soppy fairy. Fierce cannibalistic
fairies are, of course, TOTALLY cool. Long may they Twinkle, Pose,
Pounce, Flutter and Frolic through the land!

ho.

Isn't it odd how very many fine games GW produced and then "adjusted"
till they were absolutely pointless? It hurt most for Space Marine/Epic,
Talisman and Blood Bowl but the same thing basically has happened to
Warhammer and WH40K. i spose you could argue that WH/40K were cursed at
birth by Magic and ranged combat respectively, and of course it is also
true that many of the games they produced started off pants. My prize for
worst game ever would probably go to Spellfire or Wyvern but in truth the
worst game i have ever played more than once was GW's Armageddon, a
thinly-disguised WW2 Eastern Front game with the Orks as the Germans and
the Empire as the Russians. Andrew Sparkes and i ended up calling it the
Game Where You Always Win if you're the Orcs. i like Mordheim, though -
